title: 2003 HMMT February Guts Problem 23
statement: How many lattice points are enclosed by the triangle with vertices \((0,99),(5,100)\), and (2003, 500)? Don't count boundary points.

solutions.text:
0
Using the determinant formula, we get that the area of the triangle is

\[\left|\begin{array}{cc}
5 & 1 \\
2003 & 401
\end{array}\right| / 2=1\]

There are 4 lattice points on the boundary of the triangle (the three vertices and \((1004,300))\), so it follows from Pick's Theorem that there are 0 in the interior.
